NONE: B1 to like someone or something very much; to like doing something
› something that you would like to be true but that is probably not

example: She was very fond of horses.
她非常喜歡馬。
"I'm very fond of you, you know," he said.
他說：「你知道嗎，我很喜歡你。」
My brother is fond of pointing out my mistakes.
我哥哥喜歡給我挑錯。
Many of us have fond memories of our childhoods.
我們許多人都對童年懷有美好的記憶。
We said a fond farewell to each other (= we said goodbye in a loving way) and promised to write.
我們深情告別，答應給彼此寫信。
I waited at home all evening in the fond hope that he might call.
我等了一整晚，滿心期望他會打電話來。

NONE: › a thick, soft, sweet food, made mainly of sugar and used to cover cakes, or a small soft sweet made mainly from sugar
（用於裝飾糕點的）軟糖料；方旦軟糖
› to touch gently and in a loving way, or to touch in a sexual way
（充滿柔情地）撫摸，撫弄；（兩性間）愛撫

example: She fondled the puppies.
她撫摸著小狗。
He gently fondled the baby's feet.
他輕輕地撫摸著寶寶的雙腳。
She accused him of fondling her (= touching her in a sexual way) in the back of a taxi.
她指控他在計程車後排調戲她。

NONE: › in a way that shows love or great liking
› hoping that something will be true when it probably will not
（對某些可能性不大的事情）充滿希望地

example: He smiled fondly at the children.
他慈愛地對著孩子們微笑。
She fondly believed that he might come.
她天真地相信他也許會來。
George's fondness for fishing was well known.
大家都知道喬治喜歡釣魚。

NONE: › a hot dish prepared by keeping a container of either hot oil or melted cheese over a flame at the table and putting pieces of meat in the oil to be cooked or pieces of bread into the cheese

example: a cheese fondue
起司火鍋
a meat fondue
涮肉熱油火鍋

NONE: › the equipment needed to make a fondue

C: › a large container in a church, usually made of stone, that holds the water used for baptisms
› a set of letters and symbols in a particular design and size
（某種字體和字型大小的）一套鉛字，字模，字型
